''See also: [[Path of the White Fox Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|The [[Path]] of the [[White Fox]] is a sacred art primarily practiced by members of the [[Wei clan]] in [[Sacred Valley]]. Named after and inspired by the unique three-tailed [[snowfox]], the [[Path]] was established by [[Elder Whisper]], who used its power to help found the [[Wei clan]] and assimilate neighboring groups. It is characterized by the use of light and dream-based [[madra]], which allows practitioners to manipulate perceptions through illusions. These techniques can deceive the senses by twisting sound and light, creating convincing visual [[constructs]], or even mimicking scents. While the [[Path]] is highly effective for communication, acting as a messenger, or serving in roles such as teachers and artists, it is generally considered less suited for direct combat compared to more violent [[Paths]]. Practitioners often utilize specific techniques like the [[Fox Mirror]] for illusions, [[Foxfire]] for [[Striker]] attacks, or the [[Foxtail]] to blur their physical movements. Because it lacks significant offensive power, users may supplement their abilities with specialized weapons or other techniques to compensate. The [[Path]]'s essence is rooted in its ability to deceive the mind and eyes, with advanced [[Ruler techniques]] directly impacting a target's perception of reality.}}

== Unsouled ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-01-unsouled|The [[Path]] of the [[White Fox]] is the most common discipline practiced within the [[Wei clan]], followed by individuals such as Sairus. This path focuses on cultivating light and dream [[aspects]] to produce [[madra]] that twists sound and light, creates illusions, and deceives the senses. Practitioners often use Goldsteel{{!}}goldsteel to gather [[vital aura]] or utilize the [[White Fox boundary formation]] for their training, resulting in fighters who are more disciplined and stronger than those without large family support. Because the path can be tampered with to manipulate perception, it is highly disorienting, and there are even rumors that the [[Wei clan]]'s [[First Elder]] knows its [[Ruler technique]]. [[Lindon]] eventually secured a copy of this discipline through a deal with the [[First Elder]].}}
